clue.text: In church a rebellious choirboy makes a bloomer

indicators.note: the flower sits inside the run of letters across church a rebellious, so 'In' marks the concealment

explanation.surface: A naughty choirboy commits a blunder during the service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals letters concealed in 'church a rebellious'; the choirboy is surface colour. 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A harebell is a wild flowering plant, and a bloomer is crossword-speak for anything that blooms.

clue.text: If to follow, stopped in Sussex

definitions.meaning: add 'to' after the word and it means halted
a seaside town in Sussex, next to Brighton on England's south coast

explanation.surface: A traveller halts somewhere in the south of England, given a condition.
explanation.walkthrough: HOVE TO is the sailing term for bringing a ship to a stop; HOVE alone is a town joined to Brighton in East Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Hove is a town on the Sussex coast, and 'hove to' is the nautical idiom for having stopped.

clue.text: Said one was sorry for being uncivil

indicators.note: spoken out loud, a word for regret becomes a word that sounds identical

parts.note: one rued, i.e. felt regret

explanation.surface: Someone apologised for having behaved impolitely.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude behaviour is impolite, the plain synonym of uncivil.

clue.text: Queen Anne's good about field

indicators.note: the word for good wraps round the word for field, so 'about' marks the container

parts.note: bon is French for good
a ley (or lea) is a meadow or field

explanation.surface: A remark that Queen Anne is a good sort, regarding some meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link meaning 'is'; bon is French, a usual crossword source for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne, the second wife of Henry VIII, was the queen whose surname this is.

clue.text: Sussex field (frequently male) doctor in regulation of fortunate placing?

indicators.note: the run of pieces sits inside the word for regulation, so 'in' marks the insertion

parts.note: a law is a regulation
Uckfield is a Sussex town; take 'field' as the second half of its name and the first half is left
oft is an old word for often
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A rather crowded description of a Sussex field, a man, and a doctor following rules.
explanation.walkthrough: UCKFIELD is a town in East Sussex, so 'Sussex field' stands for UCK. UCK, OFT, HE and DR all go inside LAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A draw allots positions by chance, so a lucky allocation is the result of random selection.

clue.text: Joke about record one with multicoloured wear

indicators.note: the word for joke goes round the record, so 'about' marks the container

parts.note: to josh is to tease or joke
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A jest concerning a vinyl single and someone in a bright coat.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Jacob gives his son a coat of many colours, the famous multicoloured garment.

clue.text: No longer being coached in the wings?

definitions.meaning: off the stagecoach, i.e. no longer travelling by coach
out of sight of the audience at the side of a theatre stage

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the word as OFF STAGE(coach); the second is the theatre sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor waiting in the wings is out of view of the audience, beside the stage.

clue.text: Said to be absurdly officious, topped when from Brussels?

indicators.note: having its top cut off, so the first letter of the spoken form goes
spoken out loud, the officious word sounds like a B followed by the Brussels adjective

parts.note: bureaucratic describes excessive officialdom and red tape

explanation.surface: An officious EU official is mocked as ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: BUREAUCRATIC said out loud is B plus the answer; 'topped' then removes that front B.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurocrats are the officials of the European Union, whose headquarters are in Brussels.

clue.text: Art of preaching house goes a long way before marks of approval are mentioned

parts.note: a mile is proverbially a long way

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the ticks of approval sound like another word

parts.note: ticks are the marks a teacher makes for right answers

explanation.surface: A building stretches far before receiving praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes' and 'before' are linking words for the order. TICKS said out loud gives TICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Homiletics is the study and craft of composing and delivering sermons.

clue.text: Something wrong about good food shop — time given to wit

indicators.note: the word for wrongdoing goes round the shop, so 'about' marks the container

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing
a deli is a shop selling fine foods

explanation.surface: A scandal at a delicatessen, with time given to someone clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' tacks T on the end. 'To wit' looks as if it belongs with 'given', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Videlicet, abbreviated viz., is Latin for namely, introducing an example.

clue.text: Wrong French river's a very bad place for multicoloured material

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
the Oise is a river in France; the 's adds S
hell is the worst of places

explanation.surface: A French river is described as a terrible place.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortoiseshell is the mottled brown and yellow horny material from turtle shells, used decoratively.

clue.text: Opportunity to debate return of spirit

indicators.note: returning means the little word of is read backwards

parts.note: rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a chance to discuss alcohol's comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a place or meeting set aside for open discussion.

clue.text: Insincere pachyderm said to be seriously ill

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the name of the thick-skinned animal sounds like the start of the answer

parts.note: a hippo is a thick-skinned animal
a critical patient is gravely ill

explanation.surface: A dishonest elephant is reported to be in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link; HIPPO sounds like HYPO, and CRITICAL is kept as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypocritical person professes beliefs they do not hold, so is insincere.

clue.text: Favourite's definitive slogan — second class return — next to ground

indicators.note: one return turns the whole string of pieces backwards

parts.note: a pet is a favourite; the 's adds S
a motto is a slogan that defines its owner
B is the second grade

explanation.surface: A racing favourite's motto is pitted against a second-rate comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: PETS + MOTTO + B read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest stair of a flight is the one resting closest to the floor.

clue.text: See 25
Cooker for bread unopened

indicators.note: not opened means the front letter is removed

parts.note: toast is grilled bread

explanation.surface: A kitchen appliance for bread still in its wrapper.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a kiln for drying hops, a kind of oven, hence a cooker in crossword terms.

clue.text: Desire in strong man finds the opening eventually

indicators.note: the desire goes into the strong man, so 'in' marks the insertion

parts.note: Atlas, the Titan who held up the sky
to long is to desire

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Longing within a muscleman finally finds a way in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong man' is the Titan who held up the heavens in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arrived at after much delay comes eventually, finally.

clue.text: Championship engagement?

definitions.meaning: championing or support, as in taking up a cause

explanation.walkthrough: 'Championship' looks like a sporting title but means the act of championing.
explanation.definitionFit: Espousal means both adopting a cause and becoming married or betrothed.

clue.text: Back right answer to poetry crosswise

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation for right is read backwards

parts.note: verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A correct reply to a poem, given back.
explanation.definitionFit: Transverse means lying across, at right angles, exactly as crosswise does.

clue.text: Last in number 30 in the table

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone finishes last of thirty at the dinner table.
explanation.walkthrough: The table is the periodic table of elements.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is the element with atomic number thirty in the periodic table.

clue.text: Criticism about struggle with the West

parts.note: re means concerning
to vie is to compete or struggle
W is the abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: A critique concerns a fight with the western world.
explanation.definitionFit: A review is a critical appraisal of a book, play or performance.

clue.text: With oil run out, abandoned after parent became short of food

indicators.note: after puts the reworked letters and the discard behind the parent

parts.note: ma is a mother

indicators.note: out signals the letters of oil run in a disordered form

parts.note: shed means cast off

explanation.surface: Once the oil runs out, a mother leaves and goes hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges OILRUN to LNOURI; 'became' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being malnourished means lacking adequate food or nutrition.

clue.text: He says he's a Muslim leader

definitions.text: He says he's a Muslim leader

parts.note: a man speaking of himself says I'm

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A man announces that he heads a Muslim community.
explanation.walkthrough: I'M A + M (the leading letter of Muslim) spells the answer, and the whole clue defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads prayers in a mosque and is a Muslim religious leader.

clue.text: Soon to be nameless

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for shortly or presently
short for anonymous, without a name

explanation.definitionFit: Anon means shortly in old usage and is the abbreviation for anonymous.

clue.text: Scatters topless trousers

indicators.note: without its top letter, so the first letter goes

parts.note: strews means scatters

explanation.surface: Someone tosses aside trousers while bare-chested.
explanation.definitionFit: Trews are close-fitting tartan trousers traditionally worn in Scotland.

clue.text: 5's disgraceful project from her pen: a panorama — she will wallow in mud

indicators.note: the line is made from the letters of the words that follow, rearranged

explanation.surface: Joseph's shocking plan, written by her, is a vision of a woman rolling in mud.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet is Jenny Joseph (5 across), whose poem Warning begins with this line about old age and outrageous behaviour. 'from' shuffles HER PEN A PANORAMA SHE WILL WALLOW IN MUD.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's opening line sets out the speaker's plan to behave badly in old age.
